entries.proposition: WWOX mRNA is lower in 61 of 80 tumours than in the paired normal tissue (about 3.5-fold lower on the mean delta-Ct), by qPCR against G6PD, in one cohort.
entries.snippet: However, 61 of 80 tumor tissues (76.3%) showed low WWOX expression when compared to their normal counterparts (p<0.001).

entries.proposition: The same Kozak-sequence variant (minus 5 C to T) that the oral-cancer paper reads as lowering WWOX expression is present here in about 35 percent heterozygous and 9 percent homozygous tumours and 'no effect on expression' is found; the table of that comparison is not shown for this variant.
entries.snippet: However, we did not identify any effect of this alteration on the expression level.

entries.proposition: The 3'UTR variant lying in a reported miR-134 binding sequence (25 heterozygous and 10 homozygous of 65) has no effect on WWOX expression in these tumours, and miR-134 levels do not differ between tumour and normal.
entries.snippet: However, we did not observe a difference in the WWOX expression levels between the samples carrying the T or G alleles.

entries.snippet: Although there is no significant difference in the methylation frequency between the tumor and normal tissues, methylation of tumor tissue resultes in down-regulation of WWOX mRNA expression (Table 3).
